title: SLO Flight Deck: Roll-forward Orchestrator and Initiative Cadence Harmonizer
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight orchestration layer (the 'SLO Flight Deck') to harmonize initiative cadence, surface risk prior to SLO breaches, and automate safe roll-forward / rollback decisions for reliability initiatives. The feature focuses on reducing manual coordination overhead during error-budget critical windows and providing a single-pane-of-glass for PMs, SRE, and Eng to act quickly.

Background: We currently track SLO initiatives manually across spreadsheets, Linear tickets, and ad-hoc Slack threads. During tight error-budget periods teams spend engineering hours triangulating who to pause, who to throttle, and whether to run a rollback. This creates inconsistent responses and longer incident windows.

Goals:
- Provide a visible, time-series heatmap per-initiative showing forecasted error-budget burn and customer-impact staging.
- Define a small set of automated guards (gates) that can be executed: notifications, soft-throttles (routing to cheaper model variants), and canary rollback orchestration.
- Give PMs/owners a one-click 'flight action' to escalate or pause initiatives with audit trails.
- Integrate with Redwood Console telemetry, Linear initiatives, GitHub rollouts, and PagerDuty for handoffs.

Scope (MVP):
- Backend service that ingests SLI burn rates and initiative tags (from Console and Linear).
- UI card in Console called 'Flight Deck' showing per-initiative forecast, current burn % of error budget, and suggested actions.
- Two automated actions: send stakeholder escalation (Slack/PagerDuty) and trigger a 'pause' label / annotation on the linked Linear tickets.
- A templated runbook generator (Confluence link) pre-filled with context, incident links, and suggested next steps.

Out of scope (MVP):
- Automatic model variant routing or in-depth autoscaling policies (deferred to Dedicated autoscale project).
- Full rollback automation that performs infra changes (we will orchestrate the intent & human-confirmed actions).
proposal_summary:
Architecture: lightweight orchestration microservice subscribes to Console SLI streams and the initiative registry. Uses a configurable rule engine: thresholds (burn rate*window), customer-impact tiers, and runbook templates. UI surfaces suggestions and an action modal that writes annotations back to Linear and posts to Slack / PagerDuty.

Policy examples (configurable):
- Yellow: projected to hit 50% of error budget in next 72h -> notify owners and recommend slowing non-critical experiments.
- Red: projected to exhaust error budget in next 24h -> escalate on-call, add 'pause' annotation to Linear, and create runbook.

Data & telemetry: burn forecasts use exponential smoothing + Monte Carlo for a confidence band. Telemetry exported to existing observability so we can set SLI thresholds and SLO alarms.

Permissions & safety: actions default to 'suggest' mode for first two cycles; 'execute' mode requires an approver role (SRE lead or PM) and writes audit logs (required by compliance).
implementation_notes:
Phased implementation:
1) Data ingestion + initiative registry sync (2 sprints)
2) Backend rule engine + simple action hooks (2 sprints)
3) Console Flight Deck UI card + runbook template (1 sprint)
4) Pilot with SRE + Growth product (2 weeks), gather feedback, iterate.

Key integrations: Console SLI APIs, Linear API (to annotate tickets), Slack/PagerDuty webhooks, Confluence templates, GitHub PR tagging for rollouts.

Trade-offs considered:
- Automation depth: Full automation (automatic rollbacks) is high-risk and ties deeply into infra. We prioritize orchestration + human confirmation to limit blast radius.
- Forecast complexity: Monte Carlo is more accurate but heavier. Use lightweight forecasting for MVP with a gated toggle to enable Monte Carlo for teams that want more precision.

Security & privacy: Flight Deck stores initiative metadata and action audit logs. KMS-backed encryption required for stored secrets. Coordinate with Security for review if we add execute-mode for infra-affecting actions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Flight Deck UI card displays a list of active SLO-tagged initiatives and their current burn forecast with confidence bands.
2) Clicking 'Suggest Pause' posts a templated Slack + Linear annotation and creates a runbook link in Confluence.
3) System generates alerts for Yellow/Red policy thresholds and records audit entries for all actions.
4) Pilot teams report a measurable reduction in time-to-decision (target: 30% faster) during error-budget events.
5) Documentation and runbook templates exist and are reviewed by SRE and Legal.
6) Permissions controls tested: execute-mode cannot be triggered without approver role.
success_metrics:
- Mean time from detection-to-decision for SLO incidents reduced by >=30% in pilot teams.
- Number of manual cross-team coordination threads reduced by >=40% for tracked initiatives.
- Pilot satisfaction score >=4/5 from SRE and product owners.
- No unintended automated infra changes during pilot (0 incidents).
notes_for_reviewers: Reviewer asks: Is 'execute' mode necessary for MVP? Recommend delaying execute-mode for infra changes. Confirm Confluence template fields and approver role names. Validate which teams will be part of pilot (SRE and Growth recommended).
